content_units: Seasonal Allergy Pattern: Likely Explanation
Your brother’s symptoms fit   allergic rhinitis (hay fever)   more than a cold or sinus infection:
-   Supports allergies:   sneezing,   itchy eyes  , clear runny nose, 10-day duration, no fever.
-   Less suggestive of infection:   no facial pain, no thick discolored mucus, no shortness of breath.
- Common triggers include   tree, grass, or weed pollen  , dust, mold, or pet dander.
Brief context note: this is general health information, not a diagnosis.
Symptom Relief Options
Category   What it helps most   Common OTC examples   Key cautions

Intranasal steroid sprays   Best overall for nose symptoms; congestion, sneezing, drip   fluticasone, triamcinolone, budesonide   Takes consistent daily use; may cause mild nose irritation or nosebleeds
Non-drowsy oral antihistamines   Sneezing, itching, runny nose   cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine   Cetirizine can make some people sleepy
Antihistamine eye drops   Itchy, watery eyes   ketotifen, olopatadine   Remove contact lenses first if label advises
Saline nasal spray/rinse   Washes out pollen and mucus   saline spray, saline rinse kits   Use sterile/distilled/previously boiled water for rinses

Decongestants   Temporary help for stuffy nose   pseudoephedrine, phenylephrine; oxymetazoline nasal spray   Avoid or use cautiously with high blood pressure, heart issues; nasal decongestant sprays should not be used longer than 3 days
Practical take:
- For   most effective OTC approach  , many adults do best with a   daily intranasal steroid spray  .
- If   itching/sneezing   are the main issues, a   non-drowsy antihistamine   is often helpful.
- If eyes are prominent,   antihistamine eye drops   can help a lot.
Home Measures That Often Help
Option 1: Pollen avoidance routine   Reduce daily exposure, especially during high-pollen days   Best for prevention
Check pollen
Option 2: Saline rinse or spray   Clears allergens from nasal passages   Drug-free support
Nasal rinse tips
Option 3: Indoor air control   Keep windows closed, shower after being outside, change clothes, wash bedding   Helps limit ongoing exposure
Allergy basics
Useful non-medication habits:
- Shower and wash hair after outdoor time.
- Change clothes after yard work or exercise outside.
- Keep windows closed during high pollen periods.
- Use air conditioning if available.
- Avoid rubbing eyes; use cool compresses for itch relief.
- Consider sunglasses outdoors to reduce pollen contact with eyes.
When a Clinician Visit Makes Sense
Red flags or reasons to seek medical care:
-   Trouble breathing  , wheezing, chest tightness, or lip/tongue swelling.
-   Fever  , significant fatigue, or feeling generally ill.
-   Facial pain  , severe sinus pressure, tooth pain, or thick yellow/green discharge that persists.
- Symptoms lasting   weeks without improvement   or disrupting sleep/work despite OTC treatment.
- Frequent nosebleeds, severe eye swelling, vision changes, or ear pain.
- If he has conditions like   high blood pressure, glaucoma, prostate problems, or heart disease  , he should be more careful with some OTC products, especially decongestants.
